task: O3 adjudication pass for the two needs_review episodes from manual review batch 1

methodology.purpose: Resolve only the two unresolved temporal-attribution cases from O3 manual review batch 1 using higher-resolution external chronology where available.
methodology.strict_rule: A target episode can be promoted to confirmed_strict_miss only when exact-city military explosion/strike evidence can be tied to that concrete alert window by event timing or explicit during-alert wording. Publication timing alone is insufficient.
methodology.rejection_rule: Reject the target episode when the candidate source is shown to describe an event that occurred before the target window, or when the source published inside/near the target window is demonstrably cumulative reporting of impacts already known before the target and no new impact can be tied to the target window.

decisive_evidence.source: Zaporizhzhia regional prosecutor chronology, relayed by Pershyi Zaporizkyi
decisive_evidence.evidence: The Zaporizhzhia regional prosecutor's office states that the Russian UAV attack on civilian and critical infrastructure in Zaporizhzhia occurred from 18:08 to 18:24 on 20 January 2026.
decisive_evidence.temporal_relation_to_target: ends 80 minutes before target alert start

decisive_evidence.evidence: At 18:03 a UAV was reported toward Zaporizhzhia, at 18:08 an attack UAV toward Shevchenkivskyi district, PVO was reported working at 18:17, and at 18:23 one attack UAV remained over Zaporizhzhia; the all-clear followed shortly afterward.
decisive_evidence.temporal_relation_to_target: same documented attack sequence is centered around 18:08-18:24, not 19:44-20:13

decisive_evidence.evidence: The police post describes the same Shahed attack, including a strike on private housing and another strike on critical infrastructure.
decisive_evidence.temporal_relation_to_target: publication after target does not override the prosecutor-resolved event time

records.rationale: The previously unresolved 'another strike' on critical infrastructure is part of the same attack that the regional prosecutor time-bounded to 18:08-18:24. That attack ended well before the target alert began at 19:44:46. The 20:17 police publication therefore cannot be used as target-episode timing evidence.

decisive_evidence.evidence: The outlet states that as of 23:19 on 5 September at least six people had already been injured in the Zaporizhzhia drone strikes and describes the residential/civilian impacts.
decisive_evidence.temporal_relation_to_target: the six-injured impact set was already known about 31 minutes before target alert start

decisive_evidence.evidence: Independent local recap likewise states that by 23:19 at least six people had been injured and that drones had hit residential and civilian sites in different parts of Zaporizhzhia.
decisive_evidence.temporal_relation_to_target: confirms the relevant impacts pre-date the 23:49:51 target

decisive_evidence.evidence: The 23:51 article reports six injured and summarizes strikes on private/residential buildings and a non-residential administrative site while saying the UAV/KAB threat had already continued for more than two hours.
decisive_evidence.temporal_relation_to_target: secondary cumulative publication inside target, but its reported impact set was already established by 23:19

records.rationale: The 23:51 Radio Liberty timestamp initially made the five-minute target episode look plausible, but higher-resolution chronology shows that the six-injured impact set and described residential/civilian strikes were already reported by 23:19. No reviewed source identifies a new Zaporizhzhia impact between 23:49:51 and 23:54:42. The Radio Liberty item is therefore a cumulative publication-time match, not evidence of a target-window explosion.

adjudication_summary.interpretation: Both unresolved O3 candidates were false target-episode matches driven by publication timing during or shortly after a later alert. The adjudication strengthens the rule that publication time must never substitute for resolved event time on multi-episode dates.
